# google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config

Sets (creates or updates) configs of publisher models. For example, sets the request/response logging config.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](https://terraform.io/docs/providers/google/guides/provider_versions.html) for more details on beta resources.

To get more information about PublisherModelConfig, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/projects.locations.publishers.models)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs)

## Example Usage - Publisher Model Config Basic


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config" "default" {
    provider = google-beta

    publisher = "google"
    model     = "gemini-2.0-flash"
    location  = "us-central1"

    publisher_model_config {
        logging_config {
            enabled             = true
            sampling_rate       = 0.5
            bigquery_destination  {
                output_uri = "bq://my-project-name"
            }
            enable_otel_logging = true
        }
    }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `publisher_model_config` -
  (Required)
  The publisher model config.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_publisher_model_config).

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location for the model

* `publisher` -
  (Required)
  The publisher of the model

* `model` -
  (Required)
  The name of the publisher model


* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.



<a name="nested_publisher_model_config"></a>The `publisher_model_config` block supports:

* `logging_config` -
  (Optional)
  The prediction request/response logging config.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_publisher_model_config_logging_config).


<a name="nested_publisher_model_config_logging_config"></a>The `logging_config` block supports:

* `enabled` -
  (Required)
  If logging is enabled or not.

* `sampling_rate` -
  (Required)
  Percentage of requests to be logged, expressed as a fraction in range(0,1].

* `bigquery_destination` -
  (Optional)
  BigQuery table for logging. If only given a project, a new dataset will be created with
  name logging_<endpoint-display-name>_<endpoint-id> where will be made BigQuery-dataset-name
  compatible (e.g. most special characters will become underscores). If no table name is given,
  a new table will be created with name request_response_logging
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_publisher_model_config_logging_config_bigquery_destination).

* `request_response_logging_schema_version` -
  (Output)
  The schema version used in creating the BigQuery table for the request response logging.
  The versions are "v1" and "v2". The current default version is "v1".

* `enable_otel_logging` -
  (Optional)
  This field is used for large models. If true, in addition to the original large model logs,
  logs will be converted in OTel schema format, and saved in otel_log column. Default value
  is false.


<a name="nested_publisher_model_config_logging_config_bigquery_destination"></a>The `bigquery_destination` block supports:

* `output_uri` -
  (Required)
  BigQuery URI to a project or table, up to 2000 characters long. When only the project is
  specified, the Dataset and Table is created. When the full table reference is specified,
  the Dataset must exist and table must not exist.
  Accepted forms:
  BigQuery path. For example: `bq://projectId` or `bq://projectId.bqDatasetId` or
  `bq://projectId.bqDatasetId.bqTableId`.

## Import


PublisherModelConfig can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/publishers/{{publisher}}/models/{{model}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}`
* `{{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}`


In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import PublisherModelConfig using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/publishers/{{publisher}}/models/{{model}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), PublisherModelConfig can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/publishers/{{publisher}}/models/{{model}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_publisher_model_config.default {{location}}/{{publisher}}/{{model}}
```
